references.text: The same context where God explains the purpose of the plagues against Egypt - so that Pharaoh may know that there is no one like the Lord.
The Lord has created everything with a purpose, even the wicked for the day of disaster - God's sovereign purpose in raising up people.
God declares the end from the beginning and accomplishes His will - His sovereign plan and power.
God has made the earth by His great power and gives it to whom He wills - God's sovereign power over nations.
Nebuchadnezzar acknowledges that God does as He pleases with the host of heaven and the inhabitants of the earth - God's sovereign dominion.
Paul quotes this verse directly to explain God's sovereign purpose in raising up Pharaoh.
Paul elaborates on how God shows His power and makes His glory known through both vessels of wrath and vessels of mercy.
The Egyptians shall know that the Lord is God when He stretches out His hand - the purpose of displaying God's power.
The purpose of God's mighty acts is that all peoples of the earth may know that the Lord's hand is strong.
That they may know that the Lord alone is the Most High over all the earth - God's name proclaimed throughout the whole earth.
Thematic parallel: God's judgment on an enemy (Pharaoh/Gog) serves as a revelation of His power and glory to all nations.
Theological parallel: God's purpose in showing His hand/power is that the people may know and acknowledge His name.
